title: Cyrus and the Typewriter
premise: In 1911, Gideon Winterbourne, raised among pearl divers and indentured to the Meridian Trading Company, has learned that survival means being unremarkable. When a sealed letter arrives naming her family as unwitting parties to a conspiracy between colonial officials and a merchant prince now branded an enemy of the crown, she must honor a peacetime promise made to its author—a promise that now constitutes treason. As the company closes in and her loyalty to her employers collides with the truth about her father's death, Gideon smuggles the letter toward the one person who can expose the plot, discovering along the way that invisibility was always someone else's design. In the end she trades her safety for the truth, losing her place in the company but gaining a name, a history, and a future she chooses herself.
about_author: Wendell Brightwater is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing shipping ledgers from the dying days of the pearl trade. This is their second novel, written largely on a 1920s typewriter rescued from a flooded customs house.

chapters.title: The Weight of Water
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. We meet her at nineteen, diving for the company that holds her family's debt, expert at being overlooked. She catalogs cargo by day and dreams of nothing by night. Emotional beat: the quiet ache of a life built entirely around not being noticed.

chapters.title: A Letter in Wax
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. A dying diver presses a sealed letter into her hands—addressed to her family, written years ago by Elias Vane, then a company friend, now declared an enemy agent. He made her father promise to deliver it 'when peace ends.' Emotional beat: dread as the sealed wax cracks under her thumb.

chapters.title: What Father Promised
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV, with flashback chapters of her father's voice. The letter reveals her father died refusing to help officials falsify a wreck report—and that Vane kept proof. Delivering it now would brand her a traitor; destroying it betrays her father. Emotional beat: grief curdling into resolve.

chapters.title: The Company Keeps Its Books
chapters.summary: Alternating POV: Inspector Halloway of the trading company, hunting Vane's network, begins pulling records—including the Winterbourne debt. Gideon realizes her name has been in someone's ledger all along. Emotional beat: the vertigo of learning invisibility was never real.

chapters.title: Salt and Smoke
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. She seeks out Marisol, a retired diver who knew her father, and learns the promise was witnessed by half the harbor—who have all stayed silent for years out of fear. Emotional beat: solidarity kindled in a smoke-filled kitchen, the first warmth of chosen loyalty.

chapters.title: An Offer of Ink
chapters.summary: Halloway's POV. The inspector offers Gideon freedom from her indenture if she surrenders the letter and testifies against Vane. Duty, debt, and survival all point one way. Emotional beat: temptation rendered almost reasonable—the price of survival itemized in clean handwriting.

chapters.title: The Long Pier
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. She attempts a midnight handoff to Vane's courier at the pier; Halloway anticipated it. Marisol is taken instead, and Gideon escapes only because a company clerk—Tobias, who loves her quietly—looks away. Emotional beat: guilt and gratitude tangled, love complicating every calculation.

chapters.title: Enemy of the Crown
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Declared a collaborator, Gideon hides in the divers' quarter while the harbor is locked down. Tobias brings word: Halloway plans to destroy the letter and blame the Winterbournes entirely. Emotional beat: fear transmuting into fury—truth is now the only weapon left.

chapters.title: The Reading Room
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Climax. During the governor's annual audit, Gideon walks into the company's reading room and reads the letter aloud before witnesses—officials, clerks, divers summoned to witness the ledger. Halloway moves to seize it; Tobias produces the original wreck report he'd secretly copied. Emotional beat: terror and triumph in one held breath.

chapters.title: Her Own Name
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV, months later. Halloway falls, the conspiracy surfaces, and the indenture system faces inquiry. Vane, cleared, offers her a place far away; instead Gideon stays to testify for the divers' registry, signing her own name where her father once signed his mark. Emotional beat: hard-won peace—history, she finally understands, happened to her all along.
